outcome: Deliver the header an output contract declares: a dataset column whose name matches a declared name only after normalization satisfies the contract, the export writes it under the declared spelling, and no contract advice proposes a rename that the transform language would normalize back (D4)
criteria: With an open contract, a dataset column whose name equals a declared name only after normalization (case or separators, e.g. declared FirstProduct and column firstproduct) satisfies the contract check at export and in transform advice, for carried columns and for order_by and one_per keys; a normalized name that fits several dataset columns is still a mismatch

The exported file's header spells each carried column as the contract declares it, in csv (plain and formatted) and parquet; the response's columns list the header as written, and the contract evidence in the response and the audit event records each column written under another spelling (dataset name to header)

No contract advice (near_contract, reshape_to_contract) proposes a rename whose target normalizes to the column it renames; a result that differs from the contract only in spelling gets matches_contract advice

MADR 0013 records the decision; README's output-contract section says how declared names are matched and written; tests on data unrelated to any benchmark cover an aliased aggregate measure, a declared name with a space, an organizing key matched by normalization, the ambiguous case, and parquet; the test suite passes

dispositions.note: tests/test_contracts.py covers the aliased min measure, a declared 'Total Revenue' in csv and parquet, an organizing key declared as Region, the ambiguous 'UNIT PRICE', and a reshape without rename; the old renamed-problem test was rewritten for the new rule; the full suite passes except the same 8 FFmpeg tests that need libx264, absent from this host's FFmpeg

note: Chose the header-at-export option with the user over keeping the case of names in the IR (MADR 0013). verify_columns now matches through match_columns and reports an ambiguous normalized name as missing with the candidates; repair_transform only selects. The transform-time advice treats a spelling difference as a match and says how the file will spell each column. ValueRenderer also accepts a format_spec key that names the declared header exactly. Datasets and the canonical IR keep snake_case; an export without a contract is unchanged.
